Hi Vanessa,

Thanks again for the call yesterday. We're working on the contractual side for the EU→US processing flows and need to confirm which SCC module(s) Redwood intends to rely on when acting as a processor for MedSync (controller). Our procurement team is asking for the following by COB Tue (Aug 31):

- Preferred SCC module for direct controller→processor transfers (if you support Module 1 vs Module 4 decision rationale)
- Whether Redwood expects to rely on Processor→Processor modules for any subprocessors or cross-border adjacencies

- Evidence: SOC 2 summary, list of subprocessors, and a short note on key management (KMS/HSM) location

Can you confirm what you will provide and an ETA? We need to attach a short vendor memo to our DPA amendment.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — this is on the critical path for our pilot.

Date: 2026-08-29T11:02:00Z
Subject: Re: Fwd: SCCs: module preference + evidence list for our EU patient-data flow

Vanessa / Marcus — I took a quick pass on the legal side. Summary and recommended package below. Happy to draft the vendor memo once you confirm the technical points.

Recommendation (short):
- Primary: Module 1 (Controller → Processor) language for the DPA amendment. MedSync is the controller; Redwood will be a processor for the pilot workload. Module 1 is the appropriate concordance given the roles.
- Subprocessors: We expect to rely on Module 2-type wording only for downstream subprocessors when data is routed to third-party services (e.g., analytics, observability vendors). We'll call this out as "subprocessor pathway" in the memo with explicit subprocessors named.
- If MedSync requires Processor→Controller or atypical arrangements, flag and we will escalate.

Privacy/regulatory notes:
- Because the data is health-related (special category/pseudonymisation risk) add a sentence recommending MedSync confirm their DPIA conclusions; we should include a short note in the memo about our encryption-at-rest and in-transit practice, plus key management location.
- If they ask for UK-specific execution (UK addendum), we will mirror the EU choice and include the UK module equivalent in the memo.

Attachments list to produce (recommended):
1) One-page vendor memo (module recommendation + bullets) — I can draft.
2) Data-flow diagram (redwood infra regions + short storage/replication notes) — Marcus to confirm.
3) SOC 2 Type II summary (non-sensitive excerpt) — operations to provide.
4) Subprocessor list (public list) — ops.
5) Short KMS/HSM note (keys held in US; HSM provider details) — ops.

I'll prepare a legal paragraph (2–3 short bullets) explaining why Module 1 is correct and the fallback language for subprocessors. Marcus — can you confirm the data-flow PNG and whether we can share the SOC2 summary and subprocessor list to MedSync without an NDA?

-Neha
Neha Kapoor
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Compliance
[redwood.ai]

Confirming operational items. Short answers first, then attachments.

- Data-flow diagram: attached (redwood-data-flow-map-20260829.png). It shows EU ingress, optional replication to us-west-2 for burst & caching, and persistent storage flagged as region-specific buckets with customer tenancy markers.
- SOC2 Type II: we can share a one-page summary (SOC2-summary attached). Full report requires our standard confidentiality acknowledgement — we'll offer to route full report via our security portal if MedSync signs the standard NDA/procurement access form.
- Subprocessors: public list is safe to share (included in draft PDF).
- KMS/HSM: Keys are managed in customer-tenant KMS instances; master key HSM managed by Redwood in us-east-1. I'll add two sentences for the memo on KMS segregation and key rotation cadence.

Attachments I've included:
- redwood-data-flow-map-20260829.png (PNG, 245KB)
- SOC2-Type-II-summary-2026.pdf (PDF, 180KB)
- draft-sccs-selection-medsync-20260829.pdf (PDF, 52KB) — draft contains proposed Module 1 text and subprocessor clause language.

No immediate technical blockers. If MedSync insists that data must not leave EU region(s) at all, we can propose a Dedicated EU-only deployment (private tenancy) as an optional runbook; that will be a separate procurement conversation.

- Marcus

What we're recommending (short):
- Preferred SCC module: Module 1 (Controller → Processor). Rationale: MedSync is the data controller for the pilot; Redwood will process data under the DPA amendment. We will include a short fallback note for Processor→Processor subprocessors.

Evidence and deliverables (attached):
- Vendor memo (1 page) with module selection rationale and a short privacy note (attached as draft-sccs-selection-medsync-20260829.pdf).
- Data-flow diagram (redwood-data-flow-map-20260829.png) showing EU ingress, transient replication, and persistent storage markers.
- SOC2 Type II summary (SOC2-Type-II-summary-2026.pdf). We can provide the full report via our security portal under standard confidentiality access.
- Public subprocessor list included in the draft PDF.
- Short KMS/HSM note: master keys managed in us-east-1 HSMs; customer-tenant KMS per-customer (note in memo).

Operational note: If MedSync requires EU-only residency, we can support a Dedicated EU-only deployment; that'll need a short change-order and timeline (we can provide costs if you'd like to scope).

Next steps / timeline:
- Please confirm if the attached draft vendor memo and attachments are sufficient for your DPA amendment packet.
- If yes, we'll finalize the memo and supply the SOC2 portal link (or full report under NDA).
- ETA: We can provide final PDF bundle by EOD Tue (Aug 31) if we get sign-off on the draft by EOD Monday.

Feel free to call if you want to walk through the diagram.
